# Agent instructions for `lean-spherical`

## What this repository is

This repository contains Lean 4 (Mathlib) formalizations of theorems around
**spherical maximal functions**, with an emphasis on restricted and fractal
dilation sets — Stein's spherical maximal theorem, Bourgain's circular maximal
theorem, Seeger–Wainger–Wright, Mockenhaupt–Seeger–Sogge local smoothing,
Roos–Seeger, Anderson–Hughes–Roos–Seeger, Beltran–Roos–Rutar–Seeger,
Fraccaroli–Roos–Seeger, Duoandikoetxea–Vega, plus a large body of supporting
harmonic analysis (interpolation, Littlewood–Paley, Mikhlin–Hörmander,
Cotlar–Stein, Calderón–Vaillancourt, Hardy–Littlewood–Sobolev, stationary
phase, fractal dimensions, …).

Nearly all of the code — currently ~370k lines — was **machine-generated by
coding agents** (mainly Codex and Claude) across many separate formalization
efforts. Most of those efforts are finished; see `README.md` for the list of
completed results and the history of how they were produced.

You are almost certainly one more such agent. Read the rest of this file before
touching anything.

## Autoformalize skill

Agents must read and follow the `/autoformalize` skill before working in this
repository. Use the edition installed for your agent (`~/.codex/skills/autoformalize/SKILL.md`
for Codex, `~/.claude/skills/autoformalize/SKILL.md` for Claude).
Local rules in this file and the applicable project instructions take precedence
where they supersede the skill.

## The automation folder

`automation/` holds all agent-facing metadata. It is not part of the Lean
build.

* `Instructions*.md` / `instructions-*.md` — the precise standing instructions
  for one formalization effort (goal, authorized files, workflow, proof
  standards, handoff state). **When you are working on a specific project,
  its instructions file overrides the generic guidance here.**
* `Status*.md` — the status ledger for one effort: one line per step of the
  reasoning, in strict forward-reasoning order, with a status and a timestamp.
  Keep the ledger accurate and update a row *immediately* when its status
  changes, before starting the next item.
* `Report.md` — executive summary / milestone log for a project.
* `ErrorReport.md` — record of genuine errors, gaps or inconsistencies found in
  the source papers or blueprints, and of deliberate deviations from a
  blueprint. Put such observations here, not in the ledger.
* `blueprints/` — LaTeX blueprints (and their compiled PDFs) used to drive some
  of the formalizations.

Many of these files correspond to efforts that are **already finished** (e.g.
`Instructions.md` / `Status.md` for the Duoandikoetxea–Vega planar project, and
the BRRS and RS files). Do not reopen a finished project unless asked.

When the user asks you to start a **new** formalization effort and to create
instructions/status files for it, use the most recent such files — or the ones
the user points you at — as the baseline for structure and tone, and discard
everything specific to the older project.

## Where code goes

* **All agent-generated Lean code goes into `LeanSpherical/Auto/`**, unless the
  user explicitly says otherwise.
* It must live in a namespace **starting with `Auto`**, following the existing
  convention that mirrors the directory layout — e.g.
  `LeanSpherical/Auto/Spherical/FractalDilations/BRSRadial.lean` declares
  `namespace Auto.Spherical.FractalDilations.BRSRadial`,
  `LeanSpherical/Auto/CotlarStein.lean` declares `namespace Auto.CotlarStein`.
* **Do not create new files.** Work only in the files the user (or the project's
  instructions file) has named. If you believe a new file is genuinely
  necessary, stop and ask.

## Human-written code: `Definitions.lean` and `Theorems.lean`

`LeanSpherical/Definitions.lean` and `LeanSpherical/Theorems.lean` are
**human-written and must not be modified**.

The single exception: you may add (or update) the **one-line wrapper proof** of
a new or updated main theorem in `Theorems.lean`, following the existing
pattern exactly — a human-readable statement in the `Spherical` namespace whose
proof is a single application of the corresponding `Auto.*` declaration, with a
short doc comment naming the result. Nothing else in either file may change.

## Respect the existing results

The formalization results already in the repository are the value of this
repository. You may adapt existing code — generalize a hypothesis, export a
private lemma, add an import — but:

* **The existing main results must not break.** Never weaken, restate or
  `sorry` an existing theorem to make your work go through.
* `lake build` must succeed for the **whole project** after each advance, not
  just for the module you are editing.
* No `sorry`, no `admit`, no new axioms, no wrapper that assumes its own claim.
* `#print axioms` on each finished main result must report only
  `propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound`.
* A step counts as complete only when the Lean statement is mathematically
  equivalent to the source statement. A weaker hypothesis or conclusion, an
  unproved bridge, or a conditional wrapper is not completion.
* Search for existing material before writing anything: much of the groundwork
  (radial function machinery, polar coordinates, covering numbers and fractal
  dimensions, interpolation, the maximal operators themselves) already exists
  here.

## Authorship honesty

**Never present machine-generated files as human-authored.** Every file you
create or author must state, in a comment at the top,

```
This file was machine-generated by Claude.
```

(or `by Codex`, or the name of whichever coding agent is actually doing the
work). In Lean files this notice goes **below** the Copyright/License header,
before the imports. In Markdown, an HTML comment at the very top.

Existing `Auto/` files predate this rule and mostly lack the notice; that is
not a claim of human authorship — everything under `Auto/` is machine-generated
by policy. Add the notice to files you newly author; do not retrofit it across
the repository unless asked.

## Git

**Do not commit unless the user asks you to.** Leave your work in the working
tree.

When the user does ask for a commit, the message is a **single line** with a
very brief description, ideally phrased in the user's own words, otherwise
generated appropriately. It must begin with `[claude]` or `[codex]` (or the
appropriate agent name), and must list that agent as a co-author:

```
[claude] brief description of the change

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

Never rewrite history (`rebase`, `reset`, `amend`, `push --force`, …).

## Build

```
lake exe cache get!    # fetch prebuilt Mathlib
lake build             # verify the whole project
```

Toolchain and Mathlib revision are pinned in `lean-toolchain` and
`lakefile.toml`. `LeanSpherical.lean` is the root module; it imports the main
`Auto` entry points and runs `#print axioms` checks on the headline results.
